# Protein powder

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the protein powder came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as protein powder

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers protein powder in 2 forms kept separate in every comparison: protein powder, powder or ground (1,312 results) and protein powder, as sold (133 results).<sup <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-protein-powder" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-protein-powder-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of protein powder, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for protein powder

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing protein powder for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 1 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 25 µg/kg (Philips et al. 2024), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <a id="procurement-and-process-control"></a>

No maximum level for metals in protein powder was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.



<a id="finished-product-and-exposure-implications"></a>
## Exposure from protein powder

No source in the library converted protein powder concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.



<a id="requirements-evidence-assessment-and-updates"></a>
## Evidence review and remaining gaps

<a id="hmi-ing-034"></a>
<a id="which-primary-regulatory-instruments-apply-to-this-exact-ingredient-form-species-market-and-date"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-035"></a>

<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names protein powder was decided on its content: 14 occurrence extracted, 14 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Protein powder FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-protein-powder" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-protein-powder" data-question="What heavy metals are found in protein powder?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in protein powder?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, V, Se, Au, Ba, Be, Bi, Cs, Li, Mo, Pt, Rb, Ti and Tl in protein powder, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bavatharani2026-india-protein-powders-labeling-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bavatharani V, Shaw A, Sunil A, Gupta J · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bavatharani2026-india-protein-powders-labeling-metals">Labeling Transparency and Heavy Metal Contamination in Commercial Protein Powders: A Case Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Nutritions 2026; 3(2): 37-46</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bavatharani2026-india-protein-powders-labeling-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfia2020-toxic-metals-selected-foods-2018-19|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Canadian Food Inspection Agency · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfia2020-toxic-metals-selected-foods-2018-19">Toxic Metals in Selected Foods – April 1, 2018 to March 31, 2019: Food chemistry – Targeted surveys – Final report</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Food Inspection Agency</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfia2020-toxic-metals-selected-foods-2018-19">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in protein powder, as sold from 1 result in 1 reporting region, with a subgroup median of 66 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-protein-powder-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-protein-powder-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of protein powder measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of protein powder measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 36 groups of protein powder ranged from 0.8 µg/kg (retail product 31th percentile) to 88.4 µg/kg (retail product 28th percentile); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 27 groups of protein powder ranged from 28 µg/kg (retail protein product 11 (blinded code 11)) to 320 µg/kg (retail protein product 27 (blinded code 27)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/philips2024-india-protein-supplements-contaminants|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Philips CA, Theruvath AH, Ravindran R, Chopra P · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/philips2024-india-protein-supplements-contaminants">Citizens protein project: A self-funded, transparent, and concerning report on analysis of popular protein supplements sold in the Indian market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Medicine 2024;103(14):e37724</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/philips2024-india-protein-supplements-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-protein-powder" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-protein-powder" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in protein powder?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in protein powder?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same protein powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Protein powder, powder or ground (1 collection regions) had cadmium higher at 11 µg/kg, against 1.3 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (protein powder, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-protein-powder-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-protein-powder-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in protein powder is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in protein powder is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 45 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup Safety and Applied Nutrition · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2016-arsenic-rice-risk-assessment">Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Risk Assessment Report</a></span><span or ground from all samples (FDA 2013).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2016-arsenic-rice-risk-assessment|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">US Food
